paper_title: Search for Axion dark matter with the QUAX-LNF tunable haloscope
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling
notes: First results from QUAX-LNF haloscope at Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati. Cavity tuned over 6 MHz range (8.831496–8.83803 GHz) corresponding to axion mass range 36.52413–36.5511 μeV. No signal detected; 90% CL upper limit on axion-photon coupling g_agamma < 0.882 × 10^-13 GeV^-1 (reported as 0.861 × 10^-13 in abstract, 0.882 × 10^-13 in main text and conclusion; using the more precise value from main text). Local DM density ρ_a = 0.45 GeV/cm³ assumed per standard halo model. Mass-independent bound encoded as horizontal line across stated mass range. Appendix A also provides dark photon kinetic mixing limits under random polarization scenario. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 51)) | Vision: The exclusion limit plot (FIG. 7, top panel) shows the 90% single-sided C.L. upper limit for g_agamma as a function of axion mass m_a. The violet solid curve represents the expected limit in the case of no signal. The yellow region indicates the QCD axion band. The blue vertical line indicates the search presented in this paper. The QUAX-LNF experiment excludes axion dark matter in the mass range 36.52413–36.5511 μeV with axion-photon coupling g_agamma down to 0.882 × 10^-13 GeV^-1 at a C.L. of 90%. The boundary is nearly flat across the narrow mass range probed (only ~27 μeV window), consistent with a single-frequency haloscope measurement. The coupling values are read from the top panel of FIG. 7, which shows the exclusion limit as a function of mass.
